prose: Basis: Techmeme's feed summary of a Bloomberg article; the Bloomberg source fetch failed. Bloomberg reports that Nscale, the AI cloud/data-center firm, is facing investor pushback against the roughly $30 billion valuation it is targeting for its IPO, with some investors urging a lower $16-19 billion range. Adding pressure, Microsoft has exited a UK data center deal involving the company. The pushback is an early sign of public-market discipline meeting the AI infrastructure valuation surge - neocloud economics are being stress-tested before the first big listings.
highlights: Bloomberg: investors are pushing back on Nscale's ~$30B IPO valuation target
Some investors are urging a lower $16-19B valuation
Microsoft has exited a UK data center deal tied to Nscale
An early test of public-market appetite for AI infrastructure ('neocloud') valuations
